references.text: Joshua, son of Nun, was filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him, and the Israelites listened to him—a direct fulfillment of Moses giving some of his glory to his successor.
Aaron's priestly garments were to give him glory and splendor (כָּבוֹד וּלְתִפְאָרֶת), a similar concept of transferring authority and dignity to a leader.
The Lord took the Spirit that was upon Moses and placed it on the seventy elders—an earlier example of transferring spiritual authority from Moses to other leaders.
The immediate context where Moses is commanded to take Joshua, lay his hand on him, and give him some of his authority before the whole assembly.
The people confirmed they would obey Joshua just as they had obeyed Moses—evidence that the transfer of authority and glory was successful.
The Lord began to exalt Joshua in the sight of all Israel—God completed what Moses had begun by giving some of his glory to Joshua.
